lessons.title: Reading Keys
intro: A game needs a player. The KIM-1 ROM has GETCH at $1E5A: it waits for a key on the teletype and returns its character in A.
Typed digits arrive as characters: '0 to '9. Subtract '0 (SEC, SBC #'0) to turn the character into the number 0 to 9, the opposite of printing a digit.
In the quests, the keys are typed for you. Each test types different ones, so your program has to really read them. (Our board doesn't echo keys back on the paper.)

options: The character of the typed key, in A
exercises.explanation: GETCH waits for a key and puts its character into A.

exercises.prompt: The player types 4. What is A after SEC and SBC #'0?

exercises.explanation: GETCH reads a key. OUTCH ($1EA0) prints one.

exercises.prompt: How do you check if the player typed Y?
exercises.explanation: Compare the character with 'Y. Without the quote, Y would be a register name, which is an error.

exercises.prompt: This should store the typed digit as a number, but stores $35 for 5. Which line is missing something before it?
exercises.explanation: The character still has to be turned into a number: SEC, SBC #'0.

exercises.prompt: Read a key and print it back.
exercises.explanation: Read it into A, then print what's in A.

lessons.title: Random Numbers
intro: Games need surprises, but a CPU always does exactly the same thing. Programs fake randomness with a formula that jumps around so wildly it looks random.

A classic 6502 trick: shift the number right with LSR. If a 1 fell out (BCC skips if not), flip some bits with EOR #$B8. Starting from any number except 0, this visits all 255 other values before it repeats.
The starting number is called the seed. Real games took the seed from how long the player took to press a key, which is different every time.

options: 0 shifted is still 0 and nothing falls out, so it stays 0 forever
exercises.explanation: From 0, LSR gives 0 and no 1 falls into the carry. The sequence gets stuck.

options: No, it follows a fixed formula, but it looks random
exercises.explanation: Computers can't be truly random. Programmers call this pseudo-random.

options: Skips the EOR when a 0 fell out
exercises.explanation: Only when bit 0 was 1 does EOR #$B8 flip bits.

exercises.prompt: Flip the bits when a 1 fell out.
exercises.explanation: EOR flips bits. That's what scrambles the sequence.

exercises.prompt: How did real games get a different seed every time?
options: They counted how long the player waited before pressing a key
The KIM-1 had a random chip
They always used the same one
exercises.explanation: Humans are never exactly on time. That counter was the surprise.

lessons.title: The Game Loop
intro: Almost every game, from 1976 to today, has the same shape: set up, then loop forever: read the input, update the game, show what happened, check if it's over.
In 6502 terms: a few LDA/STA lines for the start values, a label GAME:, then JSR GETCH, some math and compares, JSR OUTCH or PRINT, and JMP GAME or BEQ to the end.
Keep the game's state in the zero page: the score in $30, the lives in $31, the secret number in $32. Short addresses, fast code.

output: Types !, after 3 keys or as soon as X is typed

exercises.prompt: Which order does a game loop follow?
options: Read input, update, show, check if it's over
Read all keys first, then play
exercises.explanation: Every round does the same four things.

exercises.prompt: In the example, how does the game end?
options: After 3 keys, or when X is typed
exercises.explanation: DEC $31 counts the lives down, BEQ OVER catches the X.

exercises.prompt: Go back for the next round while lives are left.
exercises.explanation: DEC sets Z when the lives reach 0. Until then, BNE jumps back.

exercises.prompt: Why is the game state in the zero page?
options: It's used all the time, and zero page instructions are shorter and faster
Only the zero page can be changed
exercises.explanation: Every round reads and writes these values.

exercises.prompt: This game never stops, even after 3 rounds. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explanation: JMP always jumps. BNE GAME stops jumping when the lives reach 0.
